# Higher-order recursive RHS allocation

Status: candidate constructive mathematics, author checks NOT_RUN; fresh independent
review and primary adjudication pending. No compiler or production authority.
Assignment: HANDLER-RECURSIVE-RHS-THEORY-20261025/r1, lane B.
Author: /root/higher_order_rec_rhs_astra_r1, requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model and effort UNKNOWN. No coauthors or descendants at author freeze.
Baseline: 03eb4b672c29f92c7bed0e2b6e4a1fbb53741c82.
Contract SHA-256: a921540d9539741dcc9dbacb9bd45f0dc086ecb97cdb03dc360dbbda1fd267eb.

## Original parent and application

GVG-REC-RHS-1 is the missing supplier in the immutable graph-extension claim at
docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:980–993, under the recursive-value
source convention and guard requirement at 180–196 and graph interpretation at
258–267. Every RHS derivation in the common recursive environment must produce
a typed closed fresh node by simultaneous substitution. The old graph's
values/types must be preserved, all recursive names must be fresh together,
and the body must use the same substitution.

The earlier restricted graph theorem accepted fresh-node typing as a premise.
It could not represent arbitrary accepted HigherOrder code, types, local binders,
result consumers, adapters or request response binders. This candidate supplies
that missing derivation for the entire accepted HigherOrder grammar.
The theorem source_rec_allocation starts from actual HigherOrder.ValueTyped RHS
derivations, independently typed outer captures, old graph typing/guard, the
actual fresh transparent-cycle criterion and the source body derivation.
It derives all fresh-node typings, allocated graph typing, its guard, and closed
body typing. It takes neither a fresh-node typing oracle nor local numeric ranks.
The finite_source_rec_allocation theorem also computes the old guard from old
finite acyclicity, eliminating numeric ranks entirely.

This applies the substitution lemmas back to the parent allocation step.
The candidate's own elaboration/review remains pending. The full paper parent
retains its original quantifiers and remains OPEN for omitted paper forms,
higher-order eliminator observation and source/native correspondence.

## Exact syntax, types and binders

HigherOrderGraphSyntax.lean defines new mutually inductive Value/Comp/Adapter
sorts parameterized by old graph names R and recursive names S. Constructors
ref r, recvar s and var i distinguish graph references, simultaneous recursive
binders and ordinary de Bruijn locals. Every accepted HigherOrder constructor is
present, recursively including code beneath lambda, delay, bind, unionCase,
scope, expose, request and both adapter positions of wrap.

The existing HigherOrder.Ty is retained exactly, including callable underneath
thunk/union/intersection and operation type arguments. The eight literal payload
domains, mode, all three lambda annotations, receipt, path correspondences,
occurrences, ordered operation type arguments and payload/response types are
retained unchanged. No opaque code label replaces a body. PathCorrespondence
retains its preexisting Prop-valued PathRule metadata; no new typing proof is
placed in syntax.

The new ValueTyped/CompTyped/AdapterTyped judgments use separate assignments
xi:R→Ty, nu:S→Ty and the ordinary local Context. A graph is R→Value R Empty.
WellTyped checks every actual closed higher-order node against xi; it does not
reuse GuardedValueGraph.NodeTyped. Graph guard is a separate conjunct in the
allocation theorem.

The mutual embedValue/Comp/Adapter functions structurally embed all accepted
syntax. Their typing theorems quantify over every original derivation and
arbitrary graph/recursive assignments. Local renaming/substitution and all three
preservation proofs cover every constructor. At a lambda, only its parameter
body lifts; its result consumer belongs to the outer environment. The consumer's
own Adapter.mk body lifts exactly once. Bind/unionCase/request each lift at their
own binder. No metadata is substituted.

## Source convention and actual RHS closing

The sourceContext nu env function represents Γ,x̄:Ā with n recursive names at
indices [0,n), and outer index i at n+i. New ordinary binders push index zero.
The source_recursive_lookup and source_outer_lookup theorems give exact lookup
equations. This is an explicit convention for the paper/accepted research
source calculus; it is not a claim about Rust runtime environment layout.

The splitNames n function maps a recursive-prefix index to recvar and an outer
index to var. The splitValue/Comp/Adapter functions first embed the actual
accepted source tree and then apply the binder-preserving local substitution.
The splitNames_typed theorem proves the lookup supplier from sourceContext;
the three split typing theorems consume it. The split_bound_zero and
split_bound_recursive equations expose behavior under a binder; repeated lifting
covers nested lambda/adapter/request/bind scopes.

The closeNamesValue/Comp/Adapter functions map all old references through Sum.inl
and all recursive names through Sum.inr simultaneously, leaving ordinary locals
alone. Their mutual typing theorem reads unchanged old types and the common
fresh assignment. CapturesTyped xi env capture independently requires each used
outer slot to contain an already closed old-graph value typed under xi.
No capture is typed by assuming a fresh graph reference exists.
The closedCapture function structurally renames these old values; closeValue,
closeComp and closeAdapter substitute them into the remaining local slots.
Their closing theorems derive closed-node/body/adapter typing.

The sourceCloseValue_typed and sourceCloseComp_typed theorems compose these
concrete operations starting at the source derivation. The sourceFresh function
uses the same construction for every RHS, with all names available together.
The named_rec_allocation theorem additionally handles explicit-name RHS syntax,
including old graph references directly in code; it supplements the actual
source-prefix supplier rather than replacing it.

## Immutable graph and exact finite guard projection

Allocation's domain is Sum R (Fin n). Old nodes are structurally renamed through
Sum.inl; fresh node s is stored at Sum.inr s. The allocation_old_node equation
preserves the entire old value/code/metadata under that renaming;
allocation_old_type preserves its exact type. The fresh_no_collision and
fresh_names_distinct theorems prove actual disjointness and fresh-name
injectivity. The old_no_fresh_edge theorem excludes old-to-fresh transparent
edges. The structural map also traverses references beneath old code/adapters.

The frontier function follows only the immediate transparent inspection chain.
References produce its successor. Both/top evidence, views and callable adapter
wrappers continue through their underlying value; none turns an alias cycle
into genuine data/lambda/delay. Literals, injections, lambda and delay terminate
inspection. References inside their fields/code remain represented and may form
guarded cycles. Free local heads are excluded by closed graph typing.

The nextValue function removes the impossible Empty recursive name.
The projectNode function maps an actual successor to GuardedValueGraph.Node.alias
and no successor to terminal token Node.unit. That unit is only an untyped guard
token: it is neither an encoding of the higher-order value nor a higher-order
type/canonical form.

The frontier_closeNames theorem connects real name constructors to successors.
The projectNode_next and projection_edge equations equate every projected
transparent edge with nextValue; fresh_edge gives exact fresh-internal edge
equivalence. The projectNode_map and project_allocation equations prove that
projection commutes with actual structural old-node renaming and allocation.

The allocationGuard definition invokes the accepted finite decision through
this equation. Local ranks are computed from FreshNoCycle; fresh-to-old edges
are permitted. The allocation_guard_iff theorem also proves necessity under the
old certificate, so the criterion is not a stronger sufficient restriction.
No restricted NodeTyped, transparent_type, reference_canonical or
no_bottom_reference theorem is applied to higher-order nodes.

## Distinguishing constructions

- The mutualRhs example consists of two actual computation-entry source lambdas.
  Each calls the opposite recursive name using its original delayed argument.
  Both read the same outer capture in body and designated result consumer.
  The mutualRhs_typed theorem proves source typing; mutualFresh_equation exposes
  allocated code, fresh targets, shared old reference and both local binders.
  The mutual_allocation theorem applies the general source theorem.
- The responseRhs example is delayed request code whose continuation reads its
  recursive node and returns the original higher-order response through a local
  bind. The response_closed equation retains operation metadata, closes payload
  capture to an old reference and recursion to a fresh reference, and retains
  response index one under that bind. Typing is derived from the source RHS.
- The oldAliasRhs example is an outer capture reference. Its allocation theorem
  admits the fresh-to-old transparent edge without an assumed local rank.
- The aliasRhs example is source x=x, typable at an arbitrary type. Its actual
  closing is a fresh self-alias; alias_cycle_rejected and
  alias_allocation_unguarded reject its guard.

These are candidate theorem instances, not executed checks or native traces.

## Source/native evidence and unchanged owners

Read-only source inspection supplies a boundary, not correspondence:

- runtime/program.rs, RuntimeProgram::from_hir_with_roots, ownership walk at
  605–646 and LocalBinding construction at 748–764, detects selected local self
  references on the lexical initializer stack and stores a recursive flag.
- runtime/machine.rs, Machine::begin_local at 2500–2545, allocates a None cell,
  extends the environment before evaluation for recursive locals, and schedules
  the initializer. Frame::Local at 1498–1560 publishes its resulting value.
- Instruction::Name at 839–861 detects recursively demanded globals or rejects
  an uninitialized local. Machine::lookup at 2585 onward traverses binder cells;
  initializer_environment preserves/extends dispatch state.

These producers/consumers are not the immutable simultaneous constructor proved
here. Their sequential initialization, mutable current-value cells, error states,
binder identities and owner/dispatch behavior need an ENV-GRAPH-1 realization
relation. A source prefix index theorem does not establish that relation.
NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE: this theory-only packet authorizes no runtime change; the
inspected producer/consumer owners have no production write lease.

No Simple-sub generation, accumulation, propagation, levels, extrusion,
qualifying intrusion or generalization is changed. No withdrawn bypass is
restored. F1/FK1, foreign-continuation, provider, residual and witness quantifiers
remain independent of this allocation result.

## Reuse, remaining premises and mutual TODOs

The accepted HigherOrder substitution proof pattern is adapted with explicit new
graph/recursive leaf cases, not assumed for extended syntax. FiniteGuardDecision
is reused exactly for its guard domain. Its accepted finite completeness result
supersedes the older graph note's historical open rank-synthesis premise.
Restricted Term/Node typing and canonical proofs are rejected as suppliers for
arbitrary HigherOrder code/types.

B-CHECK-1, primary: elaborate the frozen modules, inspect theorem signatures and
transitive axioms, then appoint a fresh nonauthor reviewer. Falsifier: a missing
accepted constructor, wrong lift, remaining fresh-node/rank oracle, forbidden
axiom or elaboration failure.

B-OBSERVE-1, next graph proof allocation: supply eliminator-directed higher-order
observation retaining wrapper/evidence context. Both/top and wrap can change the
type of an underlying transparent value; identical-type transport through the
guard projection is invalid. Falsifier: a well-typed guarded node whose claimed
canonical form loses union/intersection/top/callable evidence. OPEN.

B-PAPER-1, full-paper syntax/theory allocation: supply actual μ types and
type-changing roll/unroll/evidence, polymorphism and other omitted paper forms.
Falsifier: an accepted paper RHS without a structural typing-preserving
translation, or type-changing evidence mishandled as identity. Original paper
quantifiers remain intact.

B-NATIVE-1 / ENV-GRAPH-1, Luna/source intake: define readback/lifecycle invariants
for the inspected from_hir_with_roots, begin_local, Frame::Local, Instruction::Name
and lookup paths. A future minimal provisional instrument could record allocated
cell/binder identity, publication and the environment captured by an RHS,
retaining uninitialized reads explicitly. Falsifier: capture reads an
uninitialized/currently different cell, sequential initialization is falsely
treated as simultaneous, or a shared native value receives inconsistent types.
This is a proposed evidence TODO, not permission to edit/run the runtime.

## Freeze and resources

All 96 frozen contract dependency pins were read-only SHA-256 compared and
matched. Direct dependencies include:

- HigherOrderSyntax: ea727d33692bdcbe6b40245b960d01225b556b5334ffab649eea2699930d5972
- HigherOrderSubstitution: 19910452c45b20761ec06dc7e15f94c94b95014ff00f3f5296af005b9adf6f30

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom

import YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraphSyntax
import YulangClosure.FiniteGuardDecision

/-! Source recursive RHS allocation for the full accepted higher-order grammar.
The transparent projection is a guard certificate, never a value-typing oracle. -/
namespace YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph
open HigherOrder (Ty Context emptyContext extend ReceiptTemplate OperationInstance)

variable {R S T : Type}

def joinTy (xi : R → Ty) (nu : S → Ty) : Sum R S → Ty
  | .inl r => xi r
  | .inr s => nu s

/-- Source convention: all n recursive names occupy the nearest prefix;
outer context index i occupies index n+i. Ordinary binders extend this context
one slot at a time. This is a concrete representation of Γ,x̄:Ā. -/
def sourceContext (nu : Fin n → Ty) (env : Context) : Context := fun i =>
  if h : i < n then some (nu ⟨i, h⟩) else env (i - n)

def splitNames (n : Nat) : Nat → Value R (Fin n) := fun i =>
  if h : i < n then .recvar ⟨i, h⟩ else .var (i - n)

theorem splitNames_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty} :
    SubstitutionTyped xi nu (sourceContext nu env) env (splitNames n) := by
  intro i a hi
  by_cases h : i < n
  · simp only [sourceContext, dite_eq_left h, Option.some.injEq] at hi
    subst a
    simpa only [splitNames, dite_eq_left h] using
      (ValueTyped.recvar (xi := xi) (nu := nu) (env := env) ⟨i, h⟩)
  · simp only [sourceContext, dite_eq_right h] at hi
    simpa only [splitNames, dite_eq_right h] using (ValueTyped.var (xi := xi) (nu := nu) hi)

def splitValue (n : Nat) (v : HigherOrder.Value) : Value R (Fin n) :=
  substValue (splitNames n) (embedValue v)

def splitComp (n : Nat) (m : HigherOrder.Comp) : Comp R (Fin n) :=
  substComp (splitNames n) (embedComp m)

def splitAdapter (n : Nat) (adapter : HigherOrder.Adapter) : Adapter R (Fin n) :=
  substAdapter (splitNames n) (embedAdapter adapter)

theorem splitValue_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (h : HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext nu env) v a) :
    ValueTyped xi nu env (splitValue n v) a :=
  substValue_typed (embedValue_typed h) splitNames_typed

theorem splitComp_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (h : HigherOrder.CompTyped (sourceContext nu env) m a) :
    CompTyped xi nu env (splitComp n m) a :=
  substComp_typed (embedComp_typed h) splitNames_typed

theorem splitAdapter_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (h : HigherOrder.AdapterTyped (sourceContext nu env) adapter a b) :
    AdapterTyped xi nu env (splitAdapter n adapter) a b :=
  substAdapter_typed (embedAdapter_typed h) splitNames_typed

theorem source_recursive_lookup (nu : Fin n → Ty) (env : Context) (s : Fin n) :
    sourceContext nu env s.val = some (nu s) := by
  simp [sourceContext, s.isLt]

theorem source_outer_lookup (nu : Fin n → Ty) (env : Context) (i : Nat) :
    sourceContext nu env (n + i) = env i := by
  simp [sourceContext, Nat.not_lt.mpr (Nat.le_add_right n i)]

theorem split_recursive (s : Fin n) :
    splitNames (R := R) n s.val = .recvar s := by
  simp [splitNames, s.isLt]

theorem split_outer (i : Nat) :
    splitNames (R := R) n (n + i) = .var i := by
  simp [splitNames, Nat.not_lt.mpr (Nat.le_add_right n i)]

/-- The newly bound argument/response/input remains local index zero. -/
theorem split_bound_zero :
    lift (splitNames (R := R) n) 0 = .var 0 := rfl

theorem split_bound_recursive (s : Fin n) :
    lift (splitNames (R := R) n) (s.val + 1) = .recvar s := by
  simp [lift, split_recursive, renameValue]

/-- Closed old values can be captured independently of every fresh node. -/
def CapturesTyped (xi : R → Ty) (env : Context) (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) : Prop :=
  ∀ i a, env i = some a → ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext (capture i) a

def mapOld (f : R → T) (v : Value R Empty) : Value T Empty :=
  closeNamesValue f Empty.elim v

theorem mapOld_typed {xi : R → Ty} {tau : T → Ty}
    (f : R → T) (hf : ∀ r, tau (f r) = xi r)
    (h : ValueTyped xi emptyTy env v a) :
    ValueTyped tau emptyTy env (mapOld f v) a :=
  closeNamesValue_typed h f Empty.elim hf (fun e => Empty.elim e)

def closedCapture (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) : Nat → Value (Sum R S) Empty :=
  fun i => mapOld Sum.inl (capture i)

/-- Recursive names are closed simultaneously, then the independently typed
outer environment is substituted. No new node is used to type the captures. -/
def closeValue (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (v : Value R S) :
    Value (Sum R S) Empty :=
  substValue (closedCapture capture) (closeNamesValue Sum.inl Sum.inr v)

def closeComp (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (m : Comp R S) :
    Comp (Sum R S) Empty :=
  substComp (closedCapture capture) (closeNamesComp Sum.inl Sum.inr m)

def closeAdapter (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (adapter : Adapter R S) :
    Adapter (Sum R S) Empty :=
  substAdapter (closedCapture capture) (closeNamesAdapter Sum.inl Sum.inr adapter)

theorem closedCapture_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    SubstitutionTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy env emptyContext (closedCapture capture) := by
  intro i a hi
  exact mapOld_typed Sum.inl (fun _ => rfl) (hc i a hi)

theorem closeValue_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (h : ValueTyped xi nu env v a) (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    ValueTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (closeValue capture v) a :=
  substValue_typed
    (closeNamesValue_typed h Sum.inl Sum.inr (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl))
    (closedCapture_typed hc)

theorem closeComp_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (h : CompTyped xi nu env m a) (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (closeComp capture m) a :=
  substComp_typed
    (closeNamesComp_typed h Sum.inl Sum.inr (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl))
    (closedCapture_typed hc)

theorem closeAdapter_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (h : AdapterTyped xi nu env adapter a b) (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    AdapterTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (closeAdapter capture adapter) a b :=
  substAdapter_typed
    (closeNamesAdapter_typed h Sum.inl Sum.inr (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl))
    (closedCapture_typed hc)

def sourceCloseValue (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (n : Nat)
    (v : HigherOrder.Value) : Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty :=
  closeValue capture (splitValue n v)

def sourceCloseComp (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (n : Nat)
    (m : HigherOrder.Comp) : Comp (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty :=
  closeComp capture (splitComp n m)

theorem sourceCloseValue_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (h : HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext nu env) v a)
    (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    ValueTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (sourceCloseValue capture n v) a :=
  closeValue_typed (splitValue_typed h) hc

theorem sourceCloseComp_typed {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (h : HigherOrder.CompTyped (sourceContext nu env) m a)
    (hc : CapturesTyped xi env capture) :
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (sourceCloseComp capture n m) a :=
  closeComp_typed (splitComp_typed h) hc

abbrev Graph (R : Type) := R → Value R Empty

def WellTyped (graph : Graph R) (xi : R → Ty) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, ValueTyped xi emptyTy emptyContext (graph r) (xi r)

/-- Only genuine data introductions, lambda and delay stop transparent
inspection. Intersection/top evidence, views, and callable adapter wrappers
do not turn an alias cycle into a constructed value. Local variables cannot
occur at the head of a well-typed closed graph node. -/
def frontier : Value R S → Option (Sum R S)
  | .ref r => some (.inl r)
  | .recvar s => some (.inr s)
  | .both v | .top v | .view v _ | .wrap v _ _ => frontier v
  | _ => none

def nextValue (v : Value R Empty) : Option R :=
  (frontier v).map (Sum.elim id Empty.elim)

/-- Exact equation from the actual recursive-name constructor to the target
reference, including arbitrarily nested transparent wrappers. -/
theorem frontier_closeNames (f : R → T) (g : S → T) (v : Value R S) :
    nextValue (closeNamesValue f g v) =
      (frontier v).map (Sum.elim f g) := by
  cases v with
  | ref r => rfl
  | recvar s => rfl
  | both v => exact frontier_closeNames f g v
  | top v => exact frontier_closeNames f g v
  | view v o => exact frontier_closeNames f g v
  | wrap v i o => exact frontier_closeNames f g v
  | var i => rfl
  | unit => rfl
  | bool v => rfl
  | int v => rfl
  | floatBits v => rfl
  | string v => rfl
  | bytes v => rfl
  | path v => rfl
  | char v => rfl
  | delay m => rfl
  | inLeft v => rfl
  | inRight v => rfl
  | lambda mode receipt a b c body consumer => rfl

theorem next_mapOld (f : R → T) (v : Value R Empty) :
    nextValue (mapOld f v) = (nextValue v).map f := by
  rw [mapOld, frontier_closeNames]
  unfold nextValue
  cases h : frontier v with
  | none => rfl
  | some r =>
      cases r with
      | inl r => rfl
      | inr e => exact Empty.elim e

/-- Unit is ONLY a terminal token in the untyped guard projection. It is
never the encoding, type, or canonical form of the higher-order value. -/
def projectNode (v : Value R Empty) : GuardedValueGraph.Node R :=
  match nextValue v with
  | none => .unit
  | some r => .alias r

def projectGraph (graph : Graph R) : GuardedValueGraph.Graph R :=
  fun r => projectNode (graph r)

theorem projectNode_next (v : Value R Empty) :
    (projectNode v).next = nextValue v := by
  unfold projectNode
  cases nextValue v <;> rfl

theorem projection_edge (graph : Graph R) (r s : R) :
    (projectGraph graph r).next = some s ↔ nextValue (graph r) = some s := by
  rw [projectGraph, projectNode_next]

theorem projectNode_map (f : R → T) (v : Value R Empty) :
    projectNode (mapOld f v) = (projectNode v).map f := by
  unfold projectNode
  rw [next_mapOld]
  cases nextValue v <;> rfl

def allocate (graph : Graph R) (fresh : S → Value (Sum R S) Empty) : Graph (Sum R S)
  | .inl r => mapOld Sum.inl (graph r)
  | .inr s => fresh s

theorem allocation_old_node (graph : Graph R) (fresh : S → Value (Sum R S) Empty) (r : R) :
    allocate graph fresh (.inl r) = mapOld Sum.inl (graph r) := rfl

theorem allocation_old_type (xi : R → Ty) (nu : S → Ty) (r : R) :
    joinTy xi nu (.inl r) = xi r := rfl

theorem fresh_no_collision (r : R) (s : S) :
    (Sum.inl r : Sum R S) ≠ Sum.inr s := by intro h; cases h

theorem fresh_names_distinct {s t : S} (hne : s ≠ t) :
    (Sum.inr s : Sum R S) ≠ Sum.inr t := by
  intro h
  exact hne (Sum.inr.inj h)

theorem old_no_fresh_edge (graph : Graph R) (fresh : S → Value (Sum R S) Empty)
    (r : R) (s : S) :
    nextValue (allocate graph fresh (.inl r)) ≠ some (.inr s) := by
  change nextValue (mapOld Sum.inl (graph r)) ≠ _
  rw [next_mapOld]
  cases nextValue (graph r) <;> simp

theorem allocate_typed {graph : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : S → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped graph xi) (fresh : S → Value (Sum R S) Empty)
    (hf : ∀ s, ValueTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (fresh s) (nu s)) :
    WellTyped (allocate graph fresh) (joinTy xi nu) := by
  intro r
  cases r with
  | inl r => exact mapOld_typed Sum.inl (fun _ => rfl) (hg r)
  | inr s => exact hf s

/-- Projection commutes with the actual immutable allocation constructor. -/
theorem project_allocation (graph : Graph R) (fresh : S → Value (Sum R S) Empty) :
    projectGraph (allocate graph fresh) =
      GuardedValueGraph.allocate (projectGraph graph) (fun s => projectNode (fresh s)) := by
  funext r
  cases r with
  | inl r => exact projectNode_map Sum.inl (graph r)
  | inr s => rfl

def FreshNoCycle (fresh : Fin n → Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty) : Prop :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.FreshNoCycle (fun s => projectNode (fresh s))

theorem fresh_edge (fresh : Fin n → Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty) (s t : Fin n) :
    (GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.freshGraph (fun i => projectNode (fresh i)) s).next = some t ↔
      nextValue (fresh s) = some (.inr t) := by
  rw [GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.freshGraph_edge, projectNode_next]

/-- The finite algorithm computes the local rank from FreshNoCycle, including
fresh-to-old edges; no local rank or typing of projected units is supplied. -/
def allocationGuard {graph : Graph R} (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (fresh : Fin n → Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty) (hc : FreshNoCycle fresh) :
    GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate graph fresh)) := by
  rw [project_allocation]
  exact GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.allocateFiniteGuard guard (fun s => projectNode (fresh s)) hc

theorem allocation_guard_iff {graph : Graph R} (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (fresh : Fin n → Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty) :
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate graph fresh))) ↔ FreshNoCycle fresh := by
  rw [project_allocation]
  exact GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.allocate_guard_iff guard (fun s => projectNode (fresh s))

def sourceFresh (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (rhs : Fin n → HigherOrder.Value) :
    Fin n → Value (Sum R (Fin n)) Empty :=
  fun s => sourceCloseValue capture n (rhs s)

/-- Application to GVG-REC-RHS-1: every fresh node's typing is DERIVED from
the actual RHS derivation in the common source recursive context and separately
typed outer captures. The body uses exactly the same simultaneous substitution.
The only guard premise is the actual finite transparent-cycle criterion. -/
theorem source_rec_allocation {graph : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped graph xi) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (rhs : Fin n → HigherOrder.Value)
    (hrhs : ∀ s, HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext nu env) (rhs s) (nu s))
    (hcapture : CapturesTyped xi env capture)
    (hcycle : FreshNoCycle (sourceFresh capture rhs))
    (hbody : HigherOrder.CompTyped (sourceContext nu env) body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate graph (sourceFresh capture rhs)) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate graph (sourceFresh capture rhs)))) ∧
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (sourceCloseComp capture n body) a := by
  have hf : ∀ s, ValueTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext
      (sourceFresh capture rhs s) (nu s) :=
    fun s => sourceCloseValue_typed (hrhs s) hcapture
  exact ⟨allocate_typed hg _ hf, ⟨allocationGuard guard _ hcycle⟩,
    sourceCloseComp_typed hbody hcapture⟩

/-- The explicit-name source form also allows old graph references in RHS
code. This theorem consumes RHS derivations before closing, not pretyped fresh
nodes. The preceding theorem supplies that premise from the accepted source
grammar by the concrete prefix-splitting translation. -/
theorem named_rec_allocation {graph : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped graph xi) (guard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph graph))
    (rhs : Fin n → Value R (Fin n))
    (hrhs : ∀ s, ValueTyped xi nu env (rhs s) (nu s))
    (hcapture : CapturesTyped xi env capture)
    (hcycle : FreshNoCycle (fun s => closeValue capture (rhs s)))
    (hbody : CompTyped xi nu env body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate graph (fun s => closeValue capture (rhs s))) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded
      (projectGraph (allocate graph (fun s => closeValue capture (rhs s))))) ∧
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (closeComp capture body) a :=
  ⟨allocate_typed hg _ (fun s => closeValue_typed (hrhs s) hcapture),
    ⟨allocationGuard guard _ hcycle⟩, closeComp_typed hbody hcapture⟩

/-- For a finite old graph, neither old nor fresh numeric ranks are inputs. -/
theorem finite_source_rec_allocation {graph : Graph (Fin m)}
    {xi : Fin m → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped graph xi) (hOld : GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.NoCycle (projectGraph graph))
    (rhs : Fin n → HigherOrder.Value)
    (hrhs : ∀ s, HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext nu env) (rhs s) (nu s))
    (hcapture : CapturesTyped xi env capture)
    (hcycle : FreshNoCycle (sourceFresh capture rhs))
    (hbody : HigherOrder.CompTyped (sourceContext nu env) body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate graph (sourceFresh capture rhs)) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate graph (sourceFresh capture rhs)))) ∧
    CompTyped (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy emptyContext (sourceCloseComp capture n body) a :=
  source_rec_allocation hg (GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.guardOfNoCycle _ hOld) rhs hrhs hcapture hcycle hbody


/-- Binder equations expose the lambda consumer's separate outer scope. -/
theorem close_lambda (capture : Nat → Value R Empty)
    (mode receipt a b c body consumer) :
    closeValue (S := S) capture (.lambda mode receipt a b c body consumer) =
      .lambda mode receipt a b c
        (substComp (lift (closedCapture capture))
          (closeNamesComp Sum.inl Sum.inr body))
        (substAdapter (closedCapture capture)
          (closeNamesAdapter Sum.inl Sum.inr consumer)) := rfl

theorem close_adapter (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (a b body paths views) :
    closeAdapter (S := S) capture (.mk a b body paths views) =
      .mk a b
        (substComp (lift (closedCapture capture))
          (closeNamesComp Sum.inl Sum.inr body)) paths views := rfl

theorem close_request (capture : Nat → Value R Empty) (op payload continuation) :
    closeComp (S := S) capture (.request op payload continuation) =
      .request op (closeValue capture payload)
        (substComp (lift (closedCapture capture))
          (closeNamesComp Sum.inl Sum.inr continuation)) := rfl

namespace Examples
def unitTy : Ty := .base .unit
def functionTy : Ty := .callable unitTy unitTy
def receipt : ReceiptTemplate := ⟨[], []⟩
def outer : Context := extend emptyContext unitTy
def oldGraph : Graph (Fin 1) := fun _ => .unit
def oldTypes : Fin 1 → Ty := fun _ => unitTy
def capture : Nat → Value (Fin 1) Empty := fun _ => .ref 0

theorem old_typed : WellTyped oldGraph oldTypes := fun _ => .unit

theorem capture_typed : CapturesTyped oldTypes outer capture := by
  intro i a hi
  cases i with
  | zero =>
      change some unitTy = some a at hi
      cases hi
      exact .ref 0
  | succ i => cases hi

def oldGuard : GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph oldGraph) :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.guardOfNoCycle _
    (GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl))

def other (s : Fin 2) : Fin 2 := if s.val = 0 then 1 else 0

/-- Both source lambdas call the opposite recursive name. They share the
same outer capture in the body and in the designated result consumer. -/
def mutualRhs (s : Fin 2) : HigherOrder.Value :=
  .lambda .computation receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy
    (.bind (.ret (.var 3))
      (.dynamicCall (.var ((other s).val + 2)) (.var 1)))
    (.mk unitTy unitTy (.bind (.ret (.var 3)) (.ret (.var 1))) [] [])

theorem mutualRhs_typed (s : Fin 2) :
    HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext (fun _ : Fin 2 => functionTy) outer)
      (mutualRhs s) functionTy := by
  apply HigherOrder.ValueTyped.lambdaComputation
  · apply HigherOrder.CompTyped.bind (a := unitTy)
    · exact .ret (.var rfl)
    · exact .dynamicCall
        (.var (source_recursive_lookup (fun _ : Fin 2 => functionTy) outer (other s)))
        (.var rfl)
  · exact .mk (.bind (a := unitTy) (.ret (.var rfl)) (.ret (.var rfl)))

def mutualFresh := sourceFresh capture mutualRhs

/-- Actual allocated code, including two independent local binders and the
shared old reference. This equation is more than a pretyped reference example. -/
theorem mutualFresh_equation (s : Fin 2) :
    mutualFresh s =
      .lambda .computation receipt unitTy unitTy unitTy
        (.bind (.ret (.ref (.inl 0)))
          (.dynamicCall (.ref (.inr (other s))) (.var 1)))
        (.mk unitTy unitTy
          (.bind (.ret (.ref (.inl 0))) (.ret (.var 1))) [] []) := by
  have hs : s = 0 ∨ s = 1 := by
    have hb := s.isLt
    by_cases hz : s.val = 0
    · exact .inl (Fin.ext hz)
    · exact .inr (Fin.ext (by omega))
  rcases hs with rfl | rfl <;> rfl

theorem mutualFresh_noCycle : FreshNoCycle mutualFresh :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

theorem mutual_allocation :
    WellTyped (allocate oldGraph mutualFresh) (joinTy oldTypes (fun _ => functionTy)) ∧
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate oldGraph mutualFresh))) ∧
    CompTyped (joinTy oldTypes (fun _ => functionTy)) emptyTy emptyContext
      (sourceCloseComp capture 2 (.ret (.var 0))) functionTy :=
  source_rec_allocation old_typed oldGuard mutualRhs mutualRhs_typed capture_typed
    mutualFresh_noCycle (.ret (.var rfl))

def operation : OperationInstance := ⟨37, [functionTy], unitTy, functionTy⟩

/-- A response binder survives both recursive substitution and outer capture.
The continuation uses the recursive delayed node and returns its original
higher-order response after a local bind. -/
def responseRhs : HigherOrder.Value :=
  .delay (.request operation (.var 1)
    (.bind (.ret (.var 1)) (.ret (.var 1))))

theorem responseRhs_typed :
    HigherOrder.ValueTyped
      (sourceContext (fun _ : Fin 1 => .thunk functionTy) outer)
      responseRhs (.thunk functionTy) :=
  .delay (.request (.var rfl)
    (.bind (a := .thunk functionTy) (.ret (.var rfl)) (.ret (.var rfl))))

theorem response_closed :
    sourceCloseValue capture 1 responseRhs =
      .delay (.request operation (.ref (.inl 0))
        (.bind (.ret (.ref (.inr 0))) (.ret (.var 1)))) := rfl

theorem response_closed_typed :
    ValueTyped (joinTy oldTypes (fun _ : Fin 1 => .thunk functionTy))
      emptyTy emptyContext (sourceCloseValue capture 1 responseRhs) (.thunk functionTy) :=
  sourceCloseValue_typed responseRhs_typed capture_typed

/-- A source RHS that is an outer captured old reference is a legal
fresh-to-old transparent edge, with no rank supplied. -/
def oldAliasRhs : Fin 1 → HigherOrder.Value := fun _ => .var 1
def oldAliasFresh := sourceFresh capture oldAliasRhs

theorem oldAlias_equation (s : Fin 1) :
    oldAliasFresh s = .ref (.inl 0) := rfl

theorem oldAlias_noCycle : FreshNoCycle oldAliasFresh :=
  GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision.noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

theorem oldAlias_allocation :
    WellTyped (allocate oldGraph oldAliasFresh) (joinTy oldTypes (fun _ => unitTy)) ∧
    Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate oldGraph oldAliasFresh))) ∧
    CompTyped (joinTy oldTypes (fun _ => unitTy)) emptyTy emptyContext
      (sourceCloseComp capture 1 (.ret (.var 0))) unitTy :=
  source_rec_allocation old_typed oldGuard oldAliasRhs (fun _ => .var rfl)
    capture_typed oldAlias_noCycle (.ret (.var rfl))

def aliasRhs : Fin 1 → HigherOrder.Value := fun _ => .var 0
def aliasFresh := sourceFresh capture aliasRhs

/-- The source typing derivation alone permits x=x at any type. The separate
guard rejects this actual source-closed alias cycle. -/
theorem aliasRhs_typed (a : Ty) (s : Fin 1) :
    HigherOrder.ValueTyped (sourceContext (fun _ : Fin 1 => a) outer) (aliasRhs s) a :=
  .var rfl

theorem alias_cycle_rejected : ¬ FreshNoCycle aliasFresh := by
  intro hc
  exact hc 0 (.edge rfl)

theorem alias_allocation_unguarded :
    ¬ Nonempty (GuardedValueGraph.Guarded (projectGraph (allocate oldGraph aliasFresh))) :=
  fun h => alias_cycle_rejected ((allocation_guard_iff oldGuard aliasFresh).mp h)

end Examples

end YulangClosure.HigherOrderGraph

## Original parent and application

GVG-REC-RHS-1 is the missing supplier in the immutable graph-extension claim at
docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:980–993, under the recursive-value
source convention and guard requirement at 180–196 and graph interpretation at
258–267. Every RHS derivation in the common recursive environment must produce
a typed closed fresh node by simultaneous substitution. The old graph's
values/types must be preserved, all recursive names must be fresh together,
and the body must use the same substitution.

The earlier restricted graph theorem accepted fresh-node typing as a premise.
It could not represent arbitrary accepted HigherOrder code, types, local binders,
result consumers, adapters or request response binders. This candidate supplies
that missing derivation for the entire accepted HigherOrder grammar.
The theorem source_rec_allocation starts from actual HigherOrder.ValueTyped RHS
derivations, independently typed outer captures, old graph typing/guard, the
actual fresh transparent-cycle criterion and the source body derivation.
It derives all fresh-node typings, allocated graph typing, its guard, and closed
body typing. It takes neither a fresh-node typing oracle nor local numeric ranks.
The finite_source_rec_allocation theorem also computes the old guard from old
finite acyclicity, eliminating numeric ranks entirely.

This applies the substitution lemmas back to the parent allocation step.
The candidate's own elaboration/review remains pending. The full paper parent
retains its original quantifiers and remains OPEN for omitted paper forms,
higher-order eliminator observation and source/native correspondence.

## Exact syntax, types and binders

HigherOrderGraphSyntax.lean defines new mutually inductive Value/Comp/Adapter
sorts parameterized by old graph names R and recursive names S. Constructors
ref r, recvar s and var i distinguish graph references, simultaneous recursive
binders and ordinary de Bruijn locals. Every accepted HigherOrder constructor is
present, recursively including code beneath lambda, delay, bind, unionCase,
scope, expose, request and both adapter positions of wrap.

The existing HigherOrder.Ty is retained exactly, including callable underneath
thunk/union/intersection and operation type arguments. The eight literal payload
domains, mode, all three lambda annotations, receipt, path correspondences,
occurrences, ordered operation type arguments and payload/response types are
retained unchanged. No opaque code label replaces a body. PathCorrespondence
retains its preexisting Prop-valued PathRule metadata; no new typing proof is
placed in syntax.

The new ValueTyped/CompTyped/AdapterTyped judgments use separate assignments
xi:R→Ty, nu:S→Ty and the ordinary local Context. A graph is R→Value R Empty.
WellTyped checks every actual closed higher-order node against xi; it does not
reuse GuardedValueGraph.NodeTyped. Graph guard is a separate conjunct in the
allocation theorem.

The mutual embedValue/Comp/Adapter functions structurally embed all accepted
syntax. Their typing theorems quantify over every original derivation and
arbitrary graph/recursive assignments. Local renaming/substitution and all three
preservation proofs cover every constructor. At a lambda, only its parameter
body lifts; its result consumer belongs to the outer environment. The consumer's
own Adapter.mk body lifts exactly once. Bind/unionCase/request each lift at their
own binder. No metadata is substituted.

## Source convention and actual RHS closing

The sourceContext nu env function represents Γ,x̄:Ā with n recursive names at
indices [0,n), and outer index i at n+i. New ordinary binders push index zero.
The source_recursive_lookup and source_outer_lookup theorems give exact lookup
equations. This is an explicit convention for the paper/accepted research
source calculus; it is not a claim about Rust runtime environment layout.

The splitNames n function maps a recursive-prefix index to recvar and an outer
index to var. The splitValue/Comp/Adapter functions first embed the actual
accepted source tree and then apply the binder-preserving local substitution.
The splitNames_typed theorem proves the lookup supplier from sourceContext;
the three split typing theorems consume it. The split_bound_zero and
split_bound_recursive equations expose behavior under a binder; repeated lifting
covers nested lambda/adapter/request/bind scopes.

The closeNamesValue/Comp/Adapter functions map all old references through Sum.inl
and all recursive names through Sum.inr simultaneously, leaving ordinary locals
alone. Their mutual typing theorem reads unchanged old types and the common
fresh assignment. CapturesTyped xi env capture independently requires each used
outer slot to contain an already closed old-graph value typed under xi.
No capture is typed by assuming a fresh graph reference exists.
The closedCapture function structurally renames these old values; closeValue,
closeComp and closeAdapter substitute them into the remaining local slots.
Their closing theorems derive closed-node/body/adapter typing.

The sourceCloseValue_typed and sourceCloseComp_typed theorems compose these
concrete operations starting at the source derivation. The sourceFresh function
uses the same construction for every RHS, with all names available together.

Allocation's domain is Sum R (Fin n). Old nodes are structurally renamed through
Sum.inl; fresh node s is stored at Sum.inr s. The allocation_old_node equation
preserves the entire old value/code/metadata under that renaming;
allocation_old_type preserves its exact type. The fresh_no_collision and
fresh_names_distinct theorems prove actual disjointness and fresh-name
injectivity. The old_no_fresh_edge theorem excludes old-to-fresh transparent
edges. The structural map also traverses references beneath old code/adapters.

The frontier function follows only the immediate transparent inspection chain.
References produce its successor. Both/top evidence, views and callable adapter
wrappers continue through their underlying value; none turns an alias cycle
into genuine data/lambda/delay. Literals, injections, lambda and delay terminate

The nextValue function removes the impossible Empty recursive name.
The projectNode function maps an actual successor to GuardedValueGraph.Node.alias

The frontier_closeNames theorem connects real name constructors to successors.
The projectNode_next and projection_edge equations equate every projected

The allocationGuard definition invokes the accepted finite decision through

- The mutualRhs example consists of two actual computation-entry source lambdas.
  Each calls the opposite recursive name using its original delayed argument.

  The mutualRhs_typed theorem proves source typing; mutualFresh_equation exposes
  allocated code, fresh targets, shared old reference and both local binders.
  The mutual_allocation theorem applies the general source theorem.
- The responseRhs example is delayed request code whose continuation reads its
  recursive node and returns the original higher-order response through a local

  capture to an old reference and recursion to a fresh reference, and retains

- The oldAliasRhs example is an outer capture reference. Its allocation theorem
  admits the fresh-to-old transparent edge without an assumed local rank.
- The aliasRhs example is source x=x, typable at an arbitrary type. Its actual
  closing is a fresh self-alias; alias_cycle_rejected and

These producers/consumers are not the immutable simultaneous constructor proved

No Simple-sub generation, accumulation, propagation, levels, extrusion,

The accepted HigherOrder substitution proof pattern is adapted with explicit new

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

The parent is HO-SHALLOW-HANDLER-1, paper lines 399–456 and the local
handler/resume preservation lemma at 1069–1088. The execution theorem at
1139–1159 retains its original full syntax, graph, external-response, metadata
and arbitrary finite-prefix quantifiers. This packet supplies a candidate for
the entire accepted HigherOrder value/computation/adapter grammar, recursively
extended with handlers, ordered trials and waits. Omitted paper forms remain
outside this representation and OPEN at the parent, without changing its scope.

## Construction and application

`HigherOrderHandlerSyntax.lean` defines mutually recursive Value, Comp, Adapter,
Handler, ValueArms and OperationArms, then separate extrinsic typing judgments.
Every accepted HigherOrder constructor is copied structurally, with the same
literal payloads, modes, type annotations, operation instances, receipt data,
views and adapter path correspondence metadata. The full embedding recurses
under lambda bodies, result consumers, adapter inputs, request continuations,
binds and case branches. `embedValue_typed`, `embedComp_typed` and
`embedAdapter_typed` preserve every old typing derivation in its original context.
This is a typing embedding, not a claimed operational equivalence with the old
core's suspended-context terminal classification.

Handlers, trials and waits can occur anywhere Comp can occur, including inside
lambda/delay/adapter code. Value-arm bodies bind the returned value at index 0.
Operation-arm bodies bind payload at index 0 and K at index 1. K is concretely
encoded as a value-entry lambda, with its response binder, original code body,
and an identity result adapter. Its type is Callable(Q,A); invocation uses the
accepted delayed argument carrier convention. No assumed callable function,
opaque code label, BodyLaws or safe-attempt oracle occurs in the construction.

The six-sort renaming and substitution functions traverse all these forms.
Operation arm bodies lift twice; request continuations lift once; lambda result
consumers remain outside the lambda parameter binder. Mutual typing-preservation
proofs for renaming/substitution are supplied. `substitute_pair` closes the
payload and K simultaneously, and `attemptOperation_typed` applies it to actual
arm code. This directly supplies the local attempt premise in the parent lemma.

`HigherOrderHandlerSafety.lean` gives independent raw Step rules. A rule never
contains typing, preservation or safety as a premise. Matching compares equality
of the full OperationInstance: operation identity, ordered type arguments,
payload type and response type. Structural DecidableEq instances are derived
locally for Ty and OperationInstance; no classical equality oracle is invoked.
All arms must type-check regardless of their raw Boolean eligibility flags.
The permission meaning of these flags is not asserted.

Selection substitutes the original K into actual attempt code and puts only a
wait frame around that code. The selected handler is absent during the attempt.
No advances to the remaining arms, and Yes returns the result. Value exhaustion
produces MatchFailure; operation exhaustion forwards the same instance and
payload with `forwardedContinuation h k = handle (renameHandler succ h) k`.
This separate construction has response-to-output typing; it is not the K sent
to an arm. Request propagation under bind shifts only the ambient variables of
the bind body, preserving its own result binder.

A request inside a wait is propagated with the wait in its response binder.
The original handler, payload and remaining arms are shifted once, while the
original K is shifted under its own response binder. The pending original
instance is unchanged. Thus responding to the nested request re-enters the
pending attempt, retaining the original request and plan. Effects are not
intercepted by the removed selected handler, and no transition rewinds prior
execution. `no_after_event` retains the prior event in the prefix before No.
This is a syntactic/event-order fact, not a world-state or effect-hygiene proof.

`preservation` covers every raw step, including all base and handler transitions.
`closed_progress` covers every closed typed extended computation and gives only
Ret, Request, Fail or an actual next step. A request/failure below an evaluation
frame must propagate; it is not classified as an arbitrary suspended term.
`prefix_preservation` and `finite_prefix_safety` apply these results to every
finite raw internal prefix. `resume_typed` and `many_responses_typed` retain each
independently typed response and do not consume or modify saved K. They do not
claim the accepted old interaction arena already represents the new grammar.

Concrete applications include:

- `selected_execution`: a complete raw trace from a unit-input/bool-output
  handler through an arm that actually calls the original unit-to-unit K.
- `forwarded_execution_safe` and `distinct_continuation_types`: forwarding
  produces a unit-to-bool continuation, distinguished from selected K.
- `ordered_value_trials_safe`: a No arm followed by a Yes arm in source order.
- `wrong_identity_skipped`, `wrong_arguments_skipped`, `ineligible_skipped`:
  exact-instance/Boolean selection cases with no weakened matching relation.
- `nested_request_restoration_typed` and
  `nested_response_restoration_typed`: actual request-through-wait followed by
  any independently typed nested response.
- `nestedLambda_typed` and `nested_lambda_call_safe`: extended forms inside
  both lambda and result-adapter binders, applied back to finite-prefix safety.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.
